title: Input Tax Credit — Eligibility, Apportionment, Reversal and Blocked Credit

content.overview: Input-tax credit is available only to the extent and for the purpose the Act allows. Section 16 states eligibility. Section 17 apportions credit between business and non-business use and between taxable and exempt supplies, and it blocks credit on the enacted list. A blocked credit is not cured by a tax invoice. Apportionment and blocked credit are limits on section 16, not alternative entitlements.

cases.issue: What must a tax levy clearly identify to be valid?

cases.facts: The Court considered treaty benefits, circulars and tax avoidance arguments.
cases.issue: How should a valid tax treaty and administrative circular operate?
cases.ratioDecidendi: A treaty and valid administrative practice must be respected unless displaced by law; legitimate tax planning is not automatically evasion.

cases.name: Union of India v. Mohit Minerals Pvt. Ltd.
cases.facts: The case concerned GST levy and the legal effect of a Council recommendation.
cases.issue: What is the constitutional and statutory force of GST Council recommendations?
cases.ratioDecidendi: GST Council recommendations have persuasive value within the constitutional design but are not automatically binding as primary legislation without statutory implementation.
cases.holding: The Court interpreted the federal GST framework accordingly.
cases.relevance: Use for GST levy, delegated action and constitutional federalism.

enhancement.definition: Input-tax credit is available only to the extent and for the purpose the Act allows. Section 16 states eligibility. Section 17 apportions credit between business and non-business use and between taxable and exempt supplies, and it blocks credit on the enacted list. A blocked credit is not cured by a tax invoice.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Apportionment and blocked credit are limits on section 16, not alternative entitlements.
essentialIngredients: Credit not in the blocked list
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 17(1) and (2) restrict credit to business use and taxable supplies, including zero-rated supplies as the section treats them. Section 17(5) blocks credit for specified motor vehicles, food and similar personal consumption, works-contract construction of immovable property except in the enacted cases, and goods lost, stolen, destroyed or written off. The blocked list is statutory and should be read from the current text before advice.
examples: A manufacturer takes credit on raw materials used for taxable goods.
The same person takes credit on a car for personal use.
Section 17(5) is the block to check.
